title: A New Path: Canada and the EU Consider Closer Ties
subtitle: European leaders propose a unique 'associate membership' to strengthen cooperation as global trade tensions rise.

summary.en: The European Union has invited Canada to become its first-ever associate member. This proposal aims to deepen political and economic ties between the two partners. The move comes as both sides face increasing pressure from trade policies in the United States. While leaders express optimism, experts note that the details of this new status remain unclear. The two sides plan to meet in October to discuss the future of this partnership.
summary.zh: 歐盟已邀請加拿大成為其史上第一個準會員。此提議旨在深化雙方的政治與經濟連結。此舉是在雙方皆面臨美國貿易政策壓力日益增加的情況下所採取。儘管領導人表達樂觀，但專家指出，此新地位的細節仍不明確。雙方計畫於十月會面，討論此夥伴關係的未來。

paragraphs.en: In a major move to reshape global alliances, the European Union (EU) has officially invited Canada to become its first-ever “associate member.” This proposal was announced by European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen during her annual address in Strasbourg. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, who was present as a special guest, welcomed the idea, describing Canada and the EU as natural partners that share the same democratic values.
paragraphs.zh: 為了重塑全球聯盟，歐盟（EU）正式邀請加拿大成為其史上第一個「準會員」。這項提議是由歐盟執委會主席馮德萊恩（Ursula von der Leyen）在史特拉斯堡的年度演說中宣布。以特別嘉賓身分出席的加拿大總理卡尼（Mark Carney）對此表示歡迎，並形容加拿大與歐盟是共享民主價值的天然夥伴。

paragraphs.en: This development follows a period of growing uncertainty in international trade. According to The Guardian, both Canada and the EU have been looking for ways to strengthen their relationship as they face new challenges from the United States. Under President Donald Trump, the U.S. has raised tariffs—taxes on imported goods—and has put significant pressure on traditional allies. In response, Prime Minister Carney has sought to reduce Canada’s heavy reliance on the American market, looking instead toward Europe for a more stable economic future.
paragraphs.zh: 此一發展發生在國際貿易充滿不確定性的時期。根據《衛報》（The Guardian）報導，加拿大與歐盟在面對來自美國的新挑戰時，一直尋求加強彼此關係的方法。在川普總統領導下，美國提高了關稅（即對進口商品徵收的稅款），並對傳統盟友施加了巨大壓力。對此，卡尼總理試圖降低加拿大對美國市場的過度依賴，轉而向歐洲尋求更穩定的經濟未來。

paragraphs.en: For many in Europe, Carney has become a leading voice for countries that want to protect their interests against the influence of larger powers. As reported by NPR, Carney recently warned that some nations are using economic tools, such as supply chains and financial systems, to gain an unfair advantage. This message has resonated strongly within the European Parliament, where lawmakers gave the proposal for associate membership a warm welcome.
paragraphs.zh: 對許多歐洲人而言，卡尼已成為那些希望保護自身利益、抵禦大國影響力的國家之主要代言人。據美國國家公共廣播電台（NPR）報導，卡尼近期警告，部分國家正利用供應鏈與金融體系等經濟工具來獲取不公平的優勢。這項訊息在歐洲議會引起強烈共鳴，議員們對這項準會員資格的提議給予了熱烈歡迎。

paragraphs.en: However, the term “associate member” is new to the EU, and its exact meaning is still being debated. The EU currently has close ties with countries like Norway, Iceland, and Switzerland, but it has never created an official status for a country to be partially connected to its single market—a system that allows for the free movement of goods, services, and people. When the United Kingdom left the EU, officials were very clear that there was no middle ground between being a member and being a foreign partner. Because of this, some diplomats are cautious. One EU diplomat, cited by The Guardian, described the term as an “empty phrase” that sounds good in a speech but may be difficult to put into practice.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，「準會員」一詞對歐盟來說相當新穎，其確切含義仍在辯論中。歐盟目前與挪威、冰島和瑞士等國關係密切，但從未為一個國家創造出能部分連結其單一市場（即允許商品、服務與人員自由流動的體系）的正式地位。當英國脫離歐盟時，官員們曾明確表示，在成為會員國與成為外國夥伴之間，並不存在中間地帶。因此，部分外交官持謹慎態度。《衛報》引述一名歐盟外交官的話，形容該術語是一個「空洞的詞彙」，聽起來冠冕堂皇，但在實務上可能難以落實。

paragraphs.en: Despite these concerns, there is clear momentum for closer cooperation. The two sides already have a trade agreement, though it has not been fully approved by every EU member state. Beyond trade, the partnership is expanding into new areas. Canada has already begun working with the EU on security and defense projects, and this year it became the only non-European country allowed to join a major EU fund for joint military purchases. Von der Leyen suggested that the new associate status could lead to even deeper cooperation in areas like artificial intelligence, climate change, and the development of critical minerals and batteries.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管存在這些疑慮，雙方加強合作的動力依然明確。雙方已簽署貿易協定，儘管尚未獲得所有歐盟成員國的完全批准。除了貿易之外，夥伴關係正擴展至新領域。加拿大已開始與歐盟在安全與國防計畫上合作，今年更成為唯一獲准加入歐盟大型聯合軍事採購基金的非歐洲國家。馮德萊恩暗示，新的準會員地位可能促成在人工智慧、氣候變遷，以及關鍵礦物與電池開發等領域更深層的合作。

paragraphs.en: For those involved in the negotiations, the goal is to build a more resilient economy. Jason Wiseman, a Canadian professional working in the European Parliament, told NPR that the current political climate provides a unique opportunity to build stronger supply chains. By working together, Canada and the EU hope to secure their industries against future global shocks. The two sides are expected to meet in late October to hold a summit and begin the hard work of defining what this new partnership will actually look like.
paragraphs.zh: 對於參與談判的人士而言，目標是建立更具韌性的經濟。在歐洲議會工作的加拿大專業人士傑森·懷斯曼（Jason Wiseman）告訴 NPR，當前的政治氣候提供了一個建立更強大供應鏈的獨特機會。透過攜手合作，加拿大與歐盟希望確保其產業免受未來全球衝擊的影響。雙方預計於十月下旬舉行峰會，並開始著手定義這項新夥伴關係的具體樣貌。

paragraphs.en: As the world watches, the success of this plan will depend on whether the EU can turn these high-level promises into concrete policies. While the idea of an associate membership is popular among many lawmakers, it remains to be seen how it will be received by all 27 member states of the EU. For now, the proposal serves as a clear signal that Canada and Europe are determined to stand together in an increasingly complex global environment. Whether this leads to a formal new status or a different type of alliance, the focus remains on creating a shared space for economic security and long-term prosperity.
paragraphs.zh: 在全世界的關注下，此計畫的成功將取決於歐盟能否將這些高層承諾轉化為具體政策。雖然準會員的概念在許多議員中頗受歡迎，但它將如何被歐盟全體二十七個成員國接受，仍有待觀察。目前，這項提議傳遞出一個明確訊號，即加拿大與歐洲決心在日益複雜的全球環境中站在一起。無論這最終會演變成一種正式的新地位，還是另一種形式的聯盟，重點仍是為經濟安全與長期繁榮創造一個共享空間。

keyTerms.definitionEn: A position of compromise between two extreme or opposing views.
keyTerms.noteZh: 這是一個常見的慣用語，用來形容在兩個極端之間取得的平衡。文中：When the United Kingdom left the EU, officials were very clear that there was no middle ground between being a member and being a foreign partner.

keyTerms.definitionEn: Able to recover quickly from difficult conditions or shocks.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 有韌性的；能迅速恢復的。
keyTerms.noteZh: 此詞在商業與經濟新聞中常出現，形容經濟體在面對危機時的抗壓性。文中：For those involved in the negotiations, the goal is to build a more resilient economy.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To support each other and remain united in a difficult situation.
keyTerms.noteZh: 由動詞 stand 與副詞 together 組成，這裡強調面對挑戰時的團結。文中：For now, the proposal serves as a clear signal that Canada and Europe are determined to stand together in an increasingly complex global environment.

previousArticles.summaryEn: The European Union has invited Canada to become its first-ever 'associate member' to strengthen their political and economic ties. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen proposed the idea during her annual address, with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney in attendance. The move comes as both sides face difficult trade relations and pressure from the United States under President Trump. While the exact meaning of this new status remains unclear, both leaders hope it will lead to closer cooperation in defense, technology, and energy. Experts suggest the partnership aims to create more secure supply chains and reduce reliance on external powers.

quiz.question: According to the article, what is unique about Canada's current military involvement with the EU?

options.A: Canada is now an official member of the EU's military command structure.
options.B: Canada is the only non-European country permitted to participate in a specific EU military purchase fund.
options.C: Canada has signed a treaty to provide troops for all future EU defense operations.
options.D: Canada is leading the EU in developing new artificial intelligence for defense purposes.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第五段，文中明確提到「Canada... became the only non-European country allowed to join a major EU fund for joint military purchases」。選項 A 錯誤，因為文章並未提到加拿大成為軍事指揮結構的一員。選項 C 錯誤，文中僅提到合作，並未指明要提供所有軍事行動的兵力。選項 D 錯誤，AI 是未來潛在合作領域之一，但並非目前已經在進行的軍事資金參與。

quiz.question: Why are some EU diplomats skeptical about the proposed 'associate member' status?

options.A: They believe Canada is not democratic enough to be a partner.
options.B: They worry that Canada will eventually try to leave the EU single market.
options.C: They fear that the term lacks a clear definition and might be difficult to implement legally.
options.D: They prefer to keep the UK as an associate member instead of Canada.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據第四段，外交官們認為「associate member」是一個新詞彙，且文中引用外交官的話稱其為「empty phrase」，暗示這只是一個好聽的口號，但在實際執行層面上缺乏明確定義與可行性。選項 A 與文章內容相反，文中提到兩者分享相同的民主價值。選項 B 並非外交官擔憂的主因，他們擔憂的是該地位本身的定義模糊。選項 D 在文中完全未提及。

quiz.question: In the third paragraph, what does the word 'resonated' mean as it is used in the context of the proposal?

options.A: Caused a loud physical vibration in the parliament building.
options.B: Produced a positive reaction or sense of agreement among the lawmakers.
options.C: Caused the members to argue and disagree with each other.
options.D: Resulted in the proposal being officially rejected by the members.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。在此語境下，「resonated」意指某個觀點或訊息引起了聽眾的共鳴或認同。文中提到該訊息在歐洲議會中「resonated strongly」，隨後議會給予該提議「warm welcome」，證實了這是一種正面的支持反應。選項 A 是該詞的物理意義，在此不適用。選項 C 與文章提到的「warm welcome」衝突。選項 D 與文意相反，因為議會對此提議持正面態度。

quiz.question: What is the primary purpose of the EU and Canada's move toward an 'associate membership'?

options.A: To completely replace the current trade agreement with a new military treaty.
options.B: To force the United States to lower its tariffs on international goods.
options.C: To create a formal, legally binding union that replaces all national laws.
options.D: To strengthen economic security and cooperation in response to a changing global political environment.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 D。文章多次提到兩國合作的背景是為了應對國際貿易的不確定性、美國的壓力，以及建立更具韌性的經濟（resilient economy）。總結來說，這是為了在複雜的全球環境中尋求經濟安全與長期繁榮。選項 A 錯誤，貿易協議仍存在。選項 B 錯誤，合作是為了減少對美依賴，而非直接強迫美國降稅。選項 C 錯誤，文中並未提到要取代國家法律，僅是合作關係的深化。
